To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
zinc and benzodiazapines affect GABA mediated currents in SCN neurons.
zinc and flunitrazepan modulate GABA-mediated currents, and these modulations have the potential to affect circadian rhythms in SCN neurons.
zinc and benzodiazepam modulate GABAA-mediated synaptic currents in SCN neurons.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how the circadian system of mammals generates and maintains a 24 h rhythm in physiology and behavior.
how the circadian pacemaker of the mammalian suprachiasmic nucleus (SCN), which is responsible for generating rhythms in the brain and body, regulates the release of the neurotransmitter GABA.
the mechanisms of circadian rhythms in mammalian physiology.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Zn2+ is a potent modulator of GABAA receptors in the SCN, and the effects of Zn2+ are similar to those of the benzodiazepines.
Zn2+ modulates GABAA receptor-mediated currents in SCN neurons and that flunitrazepam modulates GABAC and GABAA receptor currents.

Zn2+ and flunitrazepan have a differential effect on the kinetics of GABAA receptor mediated currents, and this effect is dependent on the concentration of Zn2+ and the type of current being examined.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Zn2+ modulates GABAA-mediated currents and flunitrazepine prolongs GABAA receptor kinetics in suprachiasmic neurons.
the effects of Zn2+ and flunitrazepam on GABAA receptors in SCN neurons are consistent with a role for these agents in the regulation of circadian rhythms.
Zn2+ and flunitrazepan modulate SCN GABA receptors in a manner similar to their effects in the brain, but that these effects are more complex than in other brain regions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Zn2+, which is released during neuronal activity, modulates GABAA receptor function and thus can affect neuronal firing rate in the SCN.
zinc and benzodiazapine are both modulators of GABA receptors, and that zinc can increase the frequency of IPSPs in SCN neurons.
zinc is an important modulator of GABAA receptor function and can have a profound effect on the amplitude and duration of inhibitory postsynaptics currents in suprachiasmic neurons.
